shorts.title: What you will learn: File input and output
shorts.hook: Save data so it survives after the program ends.
shorts.script: Save data so it survives after the program ends. Today we save data in files. A file keeps its data after the program ends, so you can read it again later. Ofstream writes to a file. Ifstream reads from a file. You use them like cout and cin. Think of a notebook. You write in it, close it, and open it again later. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: File input and output.

shorts.title: File input and output in one minute
shorts.script: Ofstream writes to a file. Ifstream reads from a file. You use them like cout and cin. Think of a notebook. You write in it, close it, and open it again later. Ofstream opens the file for writing. It makes the file if it does not exist. We write to it with the insert operator, like cout. Close saves the data. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: File input and output in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: We write three names with marks into a file.
shorts.script: We write three names with marks into a file. The extraction operator reads one word and then one number. It works like cin. The loop ends when a read fails, at the end of the file. Each mark goes into the total. The total is ninety-one plus seventy-eight plus eighty-five, which is two hundred and fifty-four. The program prints Asha ninety-one, Ravi seventy-eight, and then two hundred and fifty-four. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A file that did not open
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in file input and output?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in file input and output? Bug of the Day. The file does not exist, but the program prints First line and nothing else. No error shows up. Always check that the file opened. A stream that fails to open gives no error. It reads nothing. Check is open, or the stream itself, before you read. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A file that did not open.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you count the lines in a file in file
shorts.script: Can you count the lines in a file in file input and output? Why did the file feel safe? Someone always closed it properly. Write a program that saves three lines to a file. Then read them back, and print how many lines you found. Write your answer in the comments. Ofstream writes to a file. Ifstream reads from a file. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
